statement_to_import_exception_handling.comment: Exception handling is built into the language and requires no imports

statement_to_start_catching_exceptions.comment: Replace `ExceptionType` with the exception class you want to catch

statement_to_catch_specific_exception.comment: Replace `ExceptionType` with the specific exception class you want to catch

statement_to_catch_multiple_exceptions.comment: Kotlin does not support multi-catch in a single block. Use separate catch blocks for each exception type.

statement_to_break_out_if_caught_excepti.comment: Kotlin does not have a dedicated statement to break out of an exception block; standard control flow (such as `return` to exit the function or `break` within a loop) is used instead

statement_to_stop_program_if_caught_exce.comment: Uses `kotlin.system.exitProcess` with an exit code to terminate the process

statement_to_start_code_if_no_exceptions.comment: Kotlin does not have an else clause for try/catch blocks

statement_to_end_trying_code.comment: The closing brace `}` ends the try block

property_with_exception_code.comment: `Throwable` in Kotlin/JVM does not define an error code property (`cause` represents the underlying causal exception, not an error code)

property_containing_other_info.comment: `Throwable` in Kotlin/JVM has no generic metadata container (such as C#'s `Exception.Data`); `suppressedExceptions` only stores suppressed exceptions from resource cleanup

invalid_data_type_exception_type.comment: Kotlin is statically typed; type mismatches are caught at compile time

variable_not_found_exception_type.comment: Variable references are resolved at compile time

key_name_not_found_exception_type.comment: Thrown when using `Map.getValue()` with a missing key

invalid_encoding_exception_type.comment: Uses the Java standard library class

overflow_exception_type.comment: Standard arithmetic operators wrap on overflow; exact math operations (such as `java.lang.Math.addExact`) throw `ArithmeticException`

floating_point_exception_type.comment: Kotlin/JVM uses IEEE 754 and returns special values (NaN, Infinity) instead of throwing exceptions

divide_by_zero_exception_type.comment: Thrown for integer division by zero. Floating-point division by zero returns Infinity or NaN.

base_memory_exception_type.comment: Uses the Java standard library class

cannot_access_pointer_exception_type.comment: Kotlin's type system helps prevent this, but it can still occur with Java interop or using the `!!` operator

base_file_exception_type.comment: Uses the Java standard library class

end_of_file_exception_type.comment: Uses the Java standard library class

file_does_not_exist_exception_type.comment: Uses the Java standard library class

file_already_exists_exception_type.comment: Uses the Java standard library class

item_is_not_a_directory_exception_type.comment: Uses the Java standard library class

cannot_access_file_exception_type.comment: Uses the Java standard library class

file_no_longer_available_exception_type.comment: Uses the Java standard library class

file_timeout_exception.comment: File operations in the JVM standard library block or fail without a specific file timeout exception

base_network_exception_type.comment: The JVM standard library has no unified base network exception class; network operations throw `java.io.IOException` or specific subclasses such as `java.net.SocketException`

connection_refused_exception_type.comment: Uses the Java standard library class

connection_broken_exception_type.comment: There is no dedicated connection broken class; standard socket operations throw `java.net.SocketException` with a message such as 'Connection reset' or 'Broken pipe'

invalid_hostname_exception.comment: Uses the Java standard library class

cannot_establish_connection_exception_ty.comment: Uses the Java standard library class

connection_timed_out_exception_type.comment: Uses the Java standard library class

bad_certificate_exception_type.comment: Base class for certificate validation and formatting errors in the Java security package

expired_certificate_exception_type.comment: Uses the Java standard library class

import_not_found_exception_type.comment: Kotlin imports are resolved at compile time; unresolved imports prevent compilation rather than throwing a runtime exception (`ClassNotFoundException` occurs during dynamic reflection or class loading)

keyboard_interrupt_exception_type.comment: Keyboard interrupts (such as Ctrl+C) send an OS signal (SIGINT) that terminates the process or triggers shutdown hooks, rather than throwing a catchable exception (`InterruptedException` is for thread interruption)

syntax_exception_type.comment: Syntax errors are caught at compile time and do not produce runtime exceptions

deprecation_warning_type.comment: Kotlin uses the `@Deprecated` annotation to mark deprecated declarations
